comments.body: STANDING-INTENT CHECK (orchestrator, pre-investigation) — the caching-collapse is DOCUMENTED, APPROVED, REVIEWED intended behavior, not an accidental regression, so remediation is a DESIGN DECISION (escalated to user), not a mechanical bug fix. Citations: (1) rebar.toml lines 190-193: 'Mixed-provider chains disable prompt caching because their provider-specific cache keys do not intersect.' (2) Authorizing ticket esthetical-earthborn-vervet (8fbd-e9d5-326e-40d8, CLOSED) that added the fallback (commit 6d4f394195b2): 'Investigation proved the existing conservative whole-chain capability intersection is intentional... Mixed Bedrock/Anthropic chains conservatively disable prompt caching because their cache styles differ.' (3) ADR 0059 §2: prompt_cache_style dispatch is 'a hard constraint, not a style preference.' => The ~2x cost is a real, large impact, but changing it REVERSES a reviewed decision. The decision hinges on one empirical fact not yet gathered: how often the Anthropic fallback ACTUALLY fires (the ticket's own Approach flags 'confirm from usage rows that the fallback almost never actually fires'). Recommend /rebar-debug Phase-1 (investigation only) to establish (i) fallback fire-rate and (ii) whether the seam can keep the primary's cache directive and drop it on an actual fallback, then approve a single direction. Options: (a) fix seam=keep hedge+restore caching [ticket default]; (b) remove fallback in rebar.toml=caching free, lose hedge; (c) accept cost=status-quo intent.

comments.body:
## /rebar-debug Phase 1 — CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE + (a)-is-safe determination

**Root cause (mechanistic, cited).** `_intersect_capabilities` (`src/rebar/llm/runner_support.py:57-73`) computes a single capability record for the WHOLE fallback chain and collapses `prompt_cache_style` to `"none"` whenever the candidates' styles disagree:
`prompt_cache_style=per_candidate[0].prompt_cache_style if len(styles) == 1 else "none"` (line 62). Since commit `6d4f394195b2` (ticket `8fbd`, 2026-08-10) configured `frontier`/`standard` as `[bedrock:…, anthropic:…]`, every such chain is mixed → style set `{"bedrock","anthropic"}` (len 2) → `"none"`. At the runner seam (`runner.py:515`) `caps = _intersect_capabilities([...])`, then `cache_settings_for(caps)` returns `None` for `"none"` (`capabilities.py:664,700,710`), so NO cache breakpoints are ever emitted — the primary Bedrock target runs uncached on every call.

**Discriminating runtime proof.**
- Ran `_intersect_capabilities` live: single `[bedrock]` chain → `prompt_cache_style="bedrock"`; mixed `[bedrock, anthropic]` → `"none"`. Confirms the collapse is the mechanism (not a config/threshold issue).
- Timeline from `.rebar/usage.jsonl` (11,902 rows): per-day cache-read fraction was 65–82% Aug 6–11, then **0.0% from Aug 12 onward** — exactly matching the mixed-chain rollout. Symptom fully explained.

**Fallback fire-rate (empirical, justifies (a)).** Provider counts across all 11,902 logged calls: `bedrock=11,851`, `anthropic=51` → the Anthropic hedge fires **0.43%** of the time. "Almost never" confirmed and quantified.

**THE decisive architectural question — is option (a) SAFE? YES.** The whole-chain intersection was justified in the code by "each style's keys are provider-specific and would error on the candidate that does not share it" (`runner.py:504`, `runner_support.py:61-62`). **That premise is false for cache keys.** Proven at runtime + by source:
- `cache_settings_for` emits provider-scoped `ModelSettings` keys (`bedrock_cache_*` vs `anthropic_cache_*`; `capabilities.py:700-714`). These flow into run-level `model_settings`.
- `pydantic_ai.settings.merge_model_settings` is a plain dict union (`base | overrides`) — NO key validation. `AnthropicModel`/`BedrockModel` read ONLY their own keys via `model_settings.get('anthropic_…')` / `.get('bedrock_…')`. A foreign key is a `.get()` miss — **silently ignored, never errored** (verified: no "Extra inputs"/unknown-setting rejection anywhere in `settings.py`/`anthropic.py`/`bedrock.py`).
- The "Bedrock rejects top-level `cache_control`" wire error (ADR 0059 §7, langchain#37042) is only produced by `AnthropicModel` code reading `anthropic_cache`; a Bedrock model never reads that key, so it cannot occur from a foreign key.

Therefore the asymmetry: **temperature/native-output/thinking CAN hard-fail cross-provider (400) and must stay conservatively intersected; prompt caching is advisory and inapplicable hints are ignored, so it can safely follow the PRIMARY.** Deriving `prompt_cache_style` from `per_candidate[0]` makes the primary Bedrock cache while a rare Anthropic fallback runs uncached-but-correct. Seam stability check: the only other consumer of the intersected `prompt_cache_style` is `structured.native_output_stack_supported` (`structured.py:161`), which is gated behind `caps.native_structured_output` (`structured.py:262`) — a field that stays conservatively intersected — so the change only affects it toward correctness for a Bedrock-primary chain, and never destabilizes provider routing. **(a) does not destabilise the seam; no escalation needed.**

**OSS best-practice grounding (per operator request).**
- **LiteLLM** models prompt caching as a per-model capability (`litellm.utils.supports_prompt_caching(model=…)`), resolved from the model that will serve — not min-intersected across a fallback set — and documents that an inapplicable/below-threshold cache directive is "**silently skipped … no error is returned**" (docs/completion/prompt_caching). This is exactly the ignored-not-errored behavior proven above.
- **pydantic-ai** (our dependency) treats capabilities/settings as a property of the RESOLVED serving model: `FallbackModel.request` re-runs `prepare_request`/`prepare_messages` per candidate, and `Model.prepare_request` merges each sub-model's OWN `.settings` (`models/fallback.py`, `models/__init__.py:340-353`).
- **LangChain #37042** (already cited in ADR 0059 §7) is the inverse anti-pattern: a shared/automatic top-level cache key broke Bedrock. It argues FOR per-resolved-provider cache keys (which rebar already emits) and AGAINST a chain-wide collapse.
The chosen fix aligns rebar with the prior-art pattern: cache capability follows the serving (primary) provider; the conservative whole-chain intersection is retained only for the fields that can genuinely error across providers.

**Defect origin / attribution.** `caused_by = 8fbd-e9d5-326e-40d8` (`esthetical-earthborn-vervet`, commit `6d4f394195b2`), **class = `plan_defect`**. The intersection code itself was introduced earlier by task `cc33` (commit `72e59d982fee`, 2026-08-02) and was correct-at-the-time — no mixed chains existed, so cache never collapsed. Per the date test, those lines PREDATE the Aug-12 behavior transition, so they did not cause it. The change that made the behavior wrong is `8fbd`, which configured the mixed-provider chain AND deliberately documented the caching loss as acceptable — a design decision whose premise (cross-provider cache keys would error) we have now proven false. `8fbd`'s reviewers are exactly who could have caught it, so it is the correct, plan-defect origin (not `cc33`, and not the fix site).

**Legitimacy:** `defect`. The current behavior is *documented/approved* intended behavior (rebar.toml ~190-193; ticket 8fbd; ADR 0059 §2), but the operator has authorized reversing that decision because its founding premise is factually wrong. Remediation therefore MUST also update the stale documented intent (rebar.toml comment + ADR 0059) as part of the same change.

Proceeding to Phase 2 (RED→GREEN, held-out oracle, mutation-checked) with option (a): minimal seam fix in `_intersect_capabilities` + doc updates.

## Plan detail moved from description (P4 oversize) — prior-art engagement + runtime soundness proof

Kept here so the description stays under the review admission limit while the reasoning remains discoverable.

**The three documented-intent sites this fix reverses (all updated in the change):**
1. `_intersect_capabilities` docstring (`runner_support.py:56-58`) — where the founding PREMISE lives: cache keys are provider-specific and "would error on the candidate that does not share it," so a mixed chain must fail closed.
2. `rebar.toml` `[llm.model_classes]` note (~190-193) — "Mixed-provider chains disable prompt caching because their provider-specific cache keys do not intersect."
3. `docs/llm-framework.md` (~829-840) — names `_intersect_capabilities` as "the authority" and restates the collapse-to-none intent.

ADR 0059 §7 does NOT assert that premise (it documents the per-provider key mechanics, the shared-automatic-key rejection / LangChain#37042, and per-model floors); it gets a superseding note so its recorded architecture matches, preserving §2's ModelProfile-not-provider-name invariant.

**The premise is false for cache keys — proven at runtime against the pinned pydantic-ai:**
- The cache directive is a set of provider-scoped `ModelSettings` keys (`capabilities.py:664-716`). `ModelSettings` is `TypedDict(total=False)` (no runtime key validation); `merge_model_settings` is a plain dict union (`base | overrides`), no validation.
- Each provider model reads ONLY its own keys via `model_settings.get('<prefix>_cache_*')`. `AnthropicModel` consults exactly four keys (`anthropic.py:1190,1580,1719,1766`); a `bedrock_cache_*` key is a silent `.get()` miss. So when the rare Anthropic fallback serves the Bedrock-primary directive it applies NO caching, adds NO top-level `cache_control`, and cannot reach the `anthropic_cache`/`anthropic_cache_messages` mutual-exclusion `UserError`: uncached-but-correct, never an error. Mirrors LiteLLM ("silently skips" an inapplicable cache directive, "no error").
- The "Bedrock rejects a top-level `cache_control`" wire error (LangChain#37042) is the OPPOSITE case: produced only by `anthropic_cache=True` reaching a Bedrock model — an Anthropic-PRIMARY chain. No rebar chain is Anthropic-primary; and a Bedrock model never reads `anthropic_cache` anyway. #37042 argues FOR per-resolved-provider keys and AGAINST a shared/automatic key — not for a chain-wide collapse.

Runtime experiment (executed): the mixed chain yields `prompt_cache_style="bedrock"`; `cache_settings_for` emits only `bedrock_cache_*`; merged into the Anthropic arm every `anthropic_cache_*` read is `None`. Codified as the parametrized `test_fallback_fires_primary_cache_directive_is_inert_on_anthropic_arm` test.

**OSS grounding:** LiteLLM = per-model `supports_prompt_caching(model=…)`, inapplicable directive silently skipped; pydantic-ai `FallbackModel` re-prepares settings per resolved candidate (capabilities are a property of the resolved serving model); LangChain#37042 is the inverse anti-pattern. All support cache-follows-serving-provider over min-intersection.

The `overlap` suggestion linking 8fbd as `duplicates` is a false positive from the shared `_intersect_capabilities` artifact: 8fbd ADDED the mixed chain (the cause, already linked `caused_by`); this ticket fixes the seam. Not a duplicate.

## Context / Problem

Daily plan-review cache reads in `.rebar/usage.jsonl` fell from ~80% of input tokens (2026-08-06..11) to 0 from 2026-08-12, and the median full plan review rose from ~$2.18 to ~$4.82 (Aug 6–29 logged spend ~$3,000). The transition coincides with commit `6d4f394195b2` (2026-08-10, ticket `esthetical-earthborn-vervet` / `8fbd-e9d5-326e-40d8`), which added the Anthropic-direct fallback to the frontier/standard classes in `rebar.toml` `[llm.model_classes]`.

`_intersect_capabilities` (`src/rebar/llm/runner_support.py`) computes ONE capability record for the whole fallback chain and collapses differing `prompt_cache_style` values to `"none"`. Both mixed chains are **Bedrock-primary, Anthropic-fallback** (`rebar.toml:223-224`), and the Anthropic hedge fires only **0.43%** of calls (51 of 11,902 logged rows), so the collapse disabled caching on the Bedrock target that serves ~99.6% of calls.

## Why reversing the documented intent is sound (detail in ticket comment)

The collapse-to-none is documented/approved intent in three sites, all updated by this change: the `_intersect_capabilities` docstring (`runner_support.py:56-58`, where the "keys would error on the non-sharing candidate" premise lives), the `rebar.toml` `[llm.model_classes]` note (~190-193), and `docs/llm-framework.md` (~829-840). ADR 0059 §7 documents the per-provider key mechanics rather than that premise; it gets a superseding note, preserving §2's ModelProfile-not-provider-name invariant.

That premise is false for cache keys, proven at runtime: the cache directive is provider-scoped `ModelSettings` keys, `merge_model_settings` is an unvalidated dict union, and each provider model reads only its own `*_cache_*` keys via `.get(...)` — so a Bedrock-primary directive reaching a served Anthropic fallback is a silent no-op (uncached-but-correct), never an error. The full mechanism, runtime experiment, LangChain#37042 direction, and OSS grounding (LiteLLM, pydantic-ai) are in the pinned ticket comment.

Therefore only `prompt_cache_style` — advisory and inert cross-provider — follows the PRIMARY; fields that CAN hard-fail cross-provider (`supports_temperature` → HTTP 400, `native_structured_output`, `supports_thinking`, `native_output_with_thinking`, `native_web_search`) stay conservatively `all(...)`-intersected.

## Approach

Option **(a): fix the capability seam** (operator decision; option (b), homogenising the chains, is off the table — the Anthropic hedge is required functionality). In `_intersect_capabilities`, derive `prompt_cache_style` from `per_candidate[0]` (the primary/serving candidate) instead of collapsing to `"none"`; keep every hard-failing field `all(...)`-intersected. Update the three stale-intent sites and ADR 0059 §7. The runtime analysis establishes (a) does not destabilise the seam, so no escalation.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner_support.py` — seam fix + docstring rewrite (stale-intent site 1).
- `tests/unit/test_runner_support.py` — NEW focused module for `_intersect_capabilities` (defined in `runner_support.py`, so this is its natural home; `test_llm_capabilities.py` imports it via the `rebar.llm.runner` re-export for unrelated native-output-under-thinking assertions, left intact).
- `rebar.toml` — `[llm.model_classes]` caching comment (site 2).
- `docs/llm-framework.md` — mixed-provider-chain caching stanza (site 3).
- `docs/adr/0059-llm-provider-seam-and-support-tiers.md` — superseding note in §7.

## Testing

Unit (`tests/unit/test_runner_support.py`): a mixed Bedrock-primary chain keeps `"bedrock"` (RED before fix); an Anthropic-primary chain keeps `"anthropic"`; a `"none"`-primary chain stays `"none"`; a homogeneous chain is unchanged; hard-fail fields still intersect conservatively; and a parametrized fallback-fires test proves the primary directive is inert on the Anthropic arm. Mutation-checked: seeding the historical collapse-to-none turns 5 of 7 tests RED. Live check: a post-fix `review-plan` logs `cache_read_tokens > 0` in `.rebar/usage.jsonl`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A regression test proves a mixed Bedrock-primary chain reports `prompt_cache_style == "bedrock"` (not `"none"`); RED before the fix, green after; runs in `make test`.
- [ ] A test proves a served Anthropic fallback receiving the Bedrock-primary directive reads every `anthropic_cache_*` key as `None` with no `UserError` (uncached-but-correct).
- [ ] A regression test asserts `supports_temperature` and `native_structured_output` still withdraw (intersect conservatively) on a mixed chain.
- [ ] The `_intersect_capabilities` docstring is updated to cache-follows-primary.
- [ ] The `rebar.toml` `[llm.model_classes]` caching comment (~190-193) is updated to cache-follows-primary.
- [ ] The `docs/llm-framework.md` caching stanza (~829-840) is updated to cache-follows-primary.
- [ ] ADR 0059 §7 carries a superseding note recording cache-follows-serving-provider.
- [ ] After the fix, a production plan review logs non-zero `cache_read_tokens` in `.rebar/usage.jsonl`.
